record.original_question: Let (X,tau) be a co-sober space and let k:(X,tau)->(X,tau) be continuous such that k:X->X is a kernel operator for the specialization order, meaning k(x) lies in the closure of {x} and k(k(x)) = k(x) for every x. Is the subspace k(X) with the subspace topology again co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. Let (X, tau) be a co-sober space and k : (X, tau) -> (X, tau) a continuous mapping for which k : X -> X is a kernel operator with respect to the specialization order of X, that is, k(x) in cl{x} and k(k(x)) = k(x) for any x in X. Is the subspace (k(X), tau|k(X)) co-sober?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a topological space $(X,\tau)$ is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset of $X$ is the closure of a unique point. Dually, $(X,\tau)$ is called co-sober if every nonempty irreducible compact saturated subset of $X$ (equivalently, every nonempty closed-under-specialization compact set that is irreducible in the cocompact sense) is the saturation of a unique point; more precisely, $(X,\tau)$ is co-sober if every irreducible closed set in the de Groot dual (the cocompact topology) is the closure (in that dual) of a unique point.

The specialization order on $(X,\tau)$ is defined by $x \le y$ iff $x \in \overline{\{y\}}$. A self-map $k : X \to X$ is called a kernel operator for the specialization order if for every $x \in X$ one has $k(x) \in \overline{\{x\}}$ (i.e., $k(x) \le x$) and $k(k(x)) = k(x)$.

Question: Let $(X,\tau)$ be a co-sober space and let $k : (X,\tau) \to (X,\tau)$ be a continuous map that is a kernel operator with respect to the specialization order of $X$. Endow the image $k(X)$ with the subspace topology $\tau|_{k(X)}$. Is $(k(X), \tau|_{k(X)})$ necessarily co-sober?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the original problem and related works on sober/co-sober spaces (including "Sober is not always co-sober" and recent work on H-sober spaces), but no source explicitly resolving whether the image of a continuous kernel operator on a co-sober space is co-sober was found. The status appears to be unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Sober is not always co-sober
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses co-sober spaces and stability properties (closed subspaces, saturated subspaces of co-sober spaces are co-sober).
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on co-sober spaces but does not resolve the kernel-operator subspace question.

status_evidence.title: The answers to some questions on H-sober spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper addressing several open problems on H-sober/co-sober spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses related open questions on H-sober spaces; not confirmed to settle the specific kernel-operator question.
